newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls to 1,020-1,040 per dlr at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls to 1,020-1,040 per dlr at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at a new historic low of 1,020-1,040 per dollar in very thin interbank volume from the morning's 950-960 and was expected to slide further amid a deepening economic crisis, dealers said.
"Banks and final clients kept bidding for dollars either for pending payments or because they expect the lev slide to go on while supply was almost nonexistent," one dealer said.
The lev closed at 935-945 on Monday.

Pressure built up on the lev at exchange bureaux and was carried over to the interbank market as people rushed to convert lev savings into foreign currency in a bid to protect them from sharp depreciation, dealers said.
Exchange shops in Sofia bought dollars at 1,020-1,050 levs in the afternoon and offered them above 1,150 against 900-960 in the morning.

A decision by the ruling Socialist party to accept a mandate for formation of a new government despite opposition protests and a presidential appeal for early elections was likely to pressure the lev to new lows in the coming days, dealers said.
"I expect political and social tensions to rise and accelerate the dollar rush, further destabilising the lev," another trader said.
The three main trade unions called a general strike from Wednesday to protest against the deepening economic crisis and back opposition calls for immediate elections.

Interior minister Nikolai Dobrev, the Socialists' nominee for premier, said after meeting President Petar Stoyanov he planned a cabinet of non-party technocrats to rescue the economy. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
